STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style plate with roasted sweet potato cubes, scrambled or soft-cooked egg whites/cheese-like pieces, and crispy bacon strips. Photographed from above at a near-top-down angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White rectangular/square-ish plate, roughly 26 cm across on its longest side. Using a ~24 cm effective diameter: area = 3.14 x 12^2 ≈ 452 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Roasted sweet potato cubes (several pieces, ~1.5-2 cm cubes)
- White scrambled egg (soft, curd-like pieces)
- Bacon strips (two pieces, cooked)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Sweet potato: ~14% of plate (≈63 cm^2)
- White egg: ~14% (≈63 cm^2)
- Bacon: ~8% (≈36 cm^2)
Total food coverage ≈ 36% of the plate, consistent with the visible scatter.

STEP 5 - Volume (outer envelope, average height):
- Sweet potato: 63 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 95 ml
- Egg: 63 cm^2 x 1.2 cm ≈ 76 ml
- Bacon: 36 cm^2 x 0.3 cm ≈ 11 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Sweet potato: 95 ml x 0.6 ≈ 57 g
- Egg: 76 ml x 0.9 ≈ 68 g
- Bacon: 11 ml x 0.9 ≈ 10 g

STEP 7 - Energy (as plated, cooked):
- Sweet potato, roasted: ~90 kcal/100 g → 57 g ≈ 51 kcal
- Scrambled egg: ~150 kcal/100 g → 68 g ≈ 102 kcal
- Bacon, cooked: ~540 kcal/100 g → 10 g ≈ 54 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 135 g and ≈ 207 kcal. This fits a modest side-portion breakfast plate with only partial coverage, so the estimate is plausible.
